findings.source_quote: ἐν γὰρ τῇ φιλοξενίᾳ εὑρίσκεται ἀγαθοποίησίς ποτε
findings.english_quote: for in hospitality one sometimes finds an opportunity for doing good
findings.issue: The source says that doing good or beneficence is sometimes found in hospitality. The English substitutes an opportunity for doing good, shifting the assertion from beneficence encountered to the possibility of beneficence. There is no separate expression for opportunity in the selected clause.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “for acts of kindness are sometimes found in hospitality,” retaining the source’s assertion and its qualification “sometimes.” This proposed wording requires fresh review before adoption.

findings.source_quote: ἐν γὰρ τῇ φιλοξενίᾳ εὑρίσκεται ἀγαθοποίησίς ποτε
findings.english_quote: because hospitality sometimes gives an opportunity to do good
findings.issue: Independently compared with the Greek, this wording changes beneficence sometimes found in hospitality into an opportunity supplied by hospitality. It preserves “sometimes” but replaces the asserted doing of good with a possibility of doing it.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “because acts of kindness are sometimes found in hospitality,” or develop another accessible rendering that retains beneficence rather than merely an opportunity. Any replacement requires fresh review.

summary: Both editions cover all twelve paragraphs and retain the selected dialogue division, necessity, negations, salvation language, practical instructions, and both concluding conditions. Reader-facing “servant” follows current policy; the restoration instruction is not homogenized into an added repentance formula. Both need a localized correction to the hospitality explanation. The notes distinguish editorial supplements and disclose substantive alternatives without replacing the selected working readings. Their external edition, plate, and manuscript reports remain unverified here: this is a separate model review of the supplied working source and disclosures, not manuscript inspection, exhaustive collation, or scholarly certification.
